title: Renewal Roadmap Deck Atelier — Standard + Enterprise QBR Templates
content:
Purpose
This is a pragmatic, modular QBR deck template set for Customer Success managers to run renewal-focused Quarterly Business Reviews for both Standard and Enterprise accounts. The goal: reduce prep time, surface measurable adoption signals, align on outcomes, and leave with a tight 8–12 week renewal sprint.

Audience
- CSMs prepping QBRs
- Renewal managers and AMs
- Solutions engineers who join technical deep dives

Design principles
- Modular: Slides are structured as independent blocks so you can reorder or omit without breaking narrative flow.
- Evidence-first: Prioritize data and examples over vague statements.
- Outcomes-oriented: Each slide ends with an explicit ask or next step to drive movement toward renewal.
- Dual-path variants: For every core slide we provide a Standard (SMB / mid-market) and Enterprise annotation (deeper legal/architecture/exec asks).

How to use
1) Pick the core flow (I. Health story -> II. Usage & value -> III. Risks & mitigations -> IV. Renewal plan).
2) Swap in Enterprise variant notes where relevant.
3) Attach the Renewal Tracker CSV (sample below) and the 12-week sprint plan as appendices.

Slide-by-slide template (compact)
1. Title + Logistics
   - Title: Customer QBR — [Account name] \u2022 [Quarter]
   - Speaker: CSM, Date, Attendees (roles)
   - Note: Add link to account Confluence page and active support case list.

2. Executive TL;DR (1 slide)
   - 3 bullets: Health (Green/Amber/Red), Trailing 3mo value snapshot, Primary ask (renewal / feature / investment).
   - Standard: Keep bullets short.
   - Enterprise: Add an explicit ask line for contractual or capacity changes and a named exec owner.

3. Business context & goals (1 slide)
   - Quick summary of customer goals, KPIs they care about, and any org changes.
   - Source: Customer kickoff notes, success plan, account plan.

4. What success looked like last quarter (2 slides)
   - Slide A: Adoption metrics (DAU/WAU, model calls, relevant feature usage).
   - Slide B: Outcomes & case studies (2–3 short customer quotes or tickets closed that delivered value).
   - Enterprise variant: Add ROI estimate (cost avoided, time saved) and stakeholder testimonials (VP/Dir).

5. Product health & quality signals (1 slide)
   - Error rates, latency percentiles, top 5 error classes, and recent incidents.
   - Add a short remediation timeline if incidents occurred.

6. Risk map (1 slide)
   - Visual: Risks columnar list (Usage, Performance, Cost, Org changes, Security/compliance).
   - For each risk include Likelihood (L/M/H) and Impact (L/M/H) and suggested mitigation.

7. Renewal posture & signals (1 slide)
   - Renewal window, renewal probability (CSM estimate), key blockers, and one-sentence ask.
   - Enterprise annotation: note legal procurement timelines and procurement contacts.

8. Roadmap alignment (1 slide)
   - Map upcoming Redwood features or Professional Services to customer priorities.
   - Enterprise variant: Include timeline for private deployment / VPC options and KMS integration steps.

9. Savings & unit economics (1 slide)
   - Token cost trends, batch/throughput improvements, and suggested optimizations (caching, quantization profile).
   - Standard: High-level cost-per-feature change.
   - Enterprise: Show expected TCO delta for proposed changes and estimated implementation effort (FTE-weeks).

10. Renewal ask & proposed terms (1 slide)
   - Proposed renewal length, financial terms (range), and recommended internal flight plan (approve/negotiation/exec review).

11. 12-week renewal sprint (1 slide)
   - Sprint plan with owners and milestones: week-by-week high-level tasks. See appendix for a template.

12. Decisions & next steps (1 slide)
   - Clear bullets: who does what by when. Include escalation path for procurement or legal.

Appendices (pick what you need)
- Renewal Tracker (CSV snippet)
- Detailed usage charts (links to Looker/Redwood Console dashboards)
- Open support & engineering tickets (linked)
- Contract history & concessions log
- Technical deep-dive slides for solutions engineers

Sample Renewal Tracker (copyable CSV)
account,renewal_date,current_term,forecast_outcome,probability_percent,key_blockers,procurement_contact
Acme Corp,2025-03-31,annual,aim_to_renew,75,capacity_limits;SLA,Marcos Diaz
BetaApps Inc,2025-02-15,monthly,negotiation,50,cost;org_reorg,Sarah Nguyen
Gamma Retail,2025-05-20,annual,exec_review,60,security_review;private_deploy,Raj Patel

12-week Renewal Sprint Template (high level)
Weeks 1-2: Align execs + confirm procurement timeline; prep legal exceptions; finalize SOW for any PS work.
Weeks 3-6: Deliver technical work (integration, performance tuning); weekly check-ins with SRE/SE.
Weeks 7-9: Business validation & ROI sign-off; run adoption campaigns; finalize pricing concessions.
Weeks 10-12: Procurement & signature; post-sign milestone kickoff; handover to onboarding/solutions.

Speaker notes & tips for CSMs
- Start with the TL;DR — busy execs want the headline within the first 60 seconds.
- Bring 1–2 customer success stories (quantified outcomes) to make benefits tangible.
- For Enterprise accounts always surface procurement timing and legal blockers early.
- Have an alternate proposal (lower-cost scope) ready in case finance pushes back.

Enterprise-specific checklist (short)
- Confirm technical owner and security reviewer contact details.
- Verify KMS/HSM and VPC requirements and any audit logs needed.
- Confirm data residency/regulatory calendar that might affect renewal timing.
- Lock in executive sponsor and schedule an exec-to-exec call if renewal probability <70%.

Operational notes for CSM team
- Templates: Keep this deck in the account Confluence page; always attach renewal tracker slice exported as CSV.
- Reporting: After the QBR, upload the finalized tracker row to CS central board (CS-4621).
- Escalation: If procurement timeline slips >2 weeks, loop in Director of Renewals and Solutions Eng.

A/B testing ideas (low lift)
- Test an ROI-first slide vs. a feature-first slide for mid-market accounts and track renewal conversion over next two quarters.
- Experiment with a 1-page executive summary (one slide) vs. standard TL;DR to see which closes faster.

Open questions / decisions needed
- Do we want a prebuilt Tableau/Looker dashboard export attached to the enterprise variant by default? (Ops cost vs. manual charting).
- Should Legal sign-off on pre-approved concession ranges live in the Confluence page?

Next steps (owner & timeline)
- CSMs to pilot this deck with 4 accounts in Nov-Dec 2024 (Owner: Priya Shah).
- Collect feedback using short post-QBR form (link in Confluence) and iterate.
- Finalize Enterprise appendix and connect with SE for technical deep-dive templates by Feb 2025.

Notes to self
- Keep slide counts lean (ideal deck size: 9–14 slides). Avoid loading execs with too many metrics; use links to drilldowns.
- Archive each QBR deck in the account folder with a 1-line renewal decision summary for searchability.

Appendix: Quick slide checklist (yes/no)
[ ] Title + attendees
[ ] Executive TL;DR
[ ] Business goals alignment
[ ] Adoption & outcomes
[ ] Product health
[ ] Risk map
[ ] Renewal posture
[ ] Roadmap alignment
[ ] Savings / TCO
[ ] Renewal ask
[ ] Sprint plan
[ ] Decisions & next steps

End of document.
